# Stellar AppKit — Full Documentation

> One SDK for every Stellar wallet — unified wallet API, Soroban built in, real transaction previews, and framework wrappers for React, Vue, Solid, and Svelte.
> 
> GitHub: https://github.com/sagantaHQ/stellar-appkit
> Docs: https://stellar-appkit.saganta.com
> npm: @saganta/stellar-appkit
> License: MIT

## What is Stellar AppKit?

Stellar AppKit is a Web3Modal / Reown AppKit equivalent for Stellar. It provides one unified wallet API, a first-class Soroban layer, real transaction previews instead of raw XDR, and a themeable UI that works identically dropped into any site.

Built by Saganta as the wallet-connection layer of its Stellar/Soroban developer infrastructure (embedded wallets, gas sponsorship, smart accounts, payment APIs).

## Key Features

### Wallet Connectivity
- Unified adapter interface aligned with SEP-43
- Freighter, Albedo, xBull, Ledger, and WalletConnect adapters
- Zero-config defaults — omit `connectors` from the config to auto-register Freighter + Albedo + xBull + Ledger. `defaultConnectors()` exported for extending the default set.
- Network mismatch recovery with auto-retry
- Cross-tab session sync via BroadcastChannel

### Transaction Preview
- Every operation decoded into plain language
- Risk flags: account-merge, signer-change, threshold-change, large-transfer, unverified-contract, broad-auth-grant
- Contract verification badges (Verified, Audited, Published by)
- Fee estimation (base fee, Soroban resource fee, total in XLM)
- Balance-delta previews from simulation stateChanges
- Auth-entry preview for standalone signAuthEntry() calls
- Signature-request queueing

### Soroban Integration
- One invoke() call: build → simulate → prepare → sign → submit → poll
- Typed contract client (ContractClient<T>) from stellar contract bindings
- RPC failover (FailoverRpcServer) with health tracking and cooldown
- Pre-simulate fee estimation (FeeEstimate)
- Auth-entry signing via authorizeEntry() — HashIdPreimage, SHA-256, ScVal wrapping
- Contract verification badges (ContractBadge)
- Balance-delta preview (decodeSimulationDeltas)

### Sign-In With Stellar (SIWS)
- Self-issued message format analogous to EIP-4361
- SEP-0053 message encoding for Freighter: sha256("Stellar Signed Message:\n" + message)
- Multi-candidate verification (8+ candidates: utf8, sha256, sha512, domain-prefixed, CRLF)
- Debug mode with diagnostics dump
- Unified signedData contract across all wallets
- Server-side verifier package (@saganta/stellar-appkit-siws-verify)

### Framework Wrappers
- React (/react): StellarAppKitProvider + hooks, useSyncExternalStore. Also exports <StellarAppKitModal> forwardRef component with onConnect/onDisconnect/onError callbacks and imperative handle (open/close/element).
- Vue (/vue): StellarAppKitPlugin + composables, shallowRef + shallowReadonly. Also exports <StellarAppKitModal> defineComponent with @connect/@disconnect/@error emits.
- Solid (/solid): StellarAppKitProvider + hooks, createSignal/createMemo. Also exports <StellarAppKitModal> component with ref callback prop.
- Svelte (/svelte): setStellarAppKitContext + stores (Svelte 4 + 5). Also exports use:stellarmodal action + openModal(node)/closeModal(node)/isStellarAppKitModal(node) helpers.
- Tree-shakable subpath exports — only ship the framework you use
- Framework modal components deliberately do NOT import the Web Component class (extends HTMLElement, undefined in pure-Node SSR). Consumers must `import '@saganta/stellar-appkit-ui-web'` once at app entry to register <stellar-appkit-modal>.
- Shared props: mode, theme, branding, logoSrc, title, autoRetryNetwork, stellarExpertAvatars
- Shared events: connect, disconnect, error (mirrors client events)
- Shared imperative handle (React/Solid/Vue via ref): open(), close(), element
- Docs: https://stellar-appkit.saganta.com/wrappers/modal-components/

### UI
- <stellar-appkit-modal> Shadow DOM Web Component
- Modal (desktop), bottom-sheet (mobile), inline (embedded) presentation
- WAAPI open/close animations — 7 presets (none, fade, scale, scale-blur, slide-up, slide-left, implode), zero dependencies, prefers-reduced-motion respected. Defaults: scale-blur for modal, slide-up for bottom-sheet.
- Draggable bottom-sheet with custom spring physics (~30 lines, native Pointer Events + requestAnimationFrame, zero dependencies)
- "Installed" badge on wallet list — accent-colored pill marking ready-to-use wallets
- Wallet-provided avatars + gradient fallback + Stellar Expert avatars
- Copy-to-clipboard on all address displays
- Conic-gradient loading spinner
- Sleek custom scrollbar (hover-show, theme-aware)
- Connected view: XLM balance, transaction history, explorer links, network pill, overflow menu

## Installation

```bash
npm install @saganta/stellar-appkit @saganta/stellar-appkit-ui-web
```

All wallet SDKs (@stellar/stellar-sdk, @stellar/freighter-api, @albedo-link/intent, @creit.tech/xbull-wallet-connect, @ledgerhq/*, @walletconnect/sign-client) are bundled as regular dependencies — installed automatically, version-locked, tree-shaken if unused. The UI package has zero runtime dependencies (custom spring + WAAPI). Frameworks (react, vue, solid-js, svelte) are optional peer dependencies.

## Quick Start

```ts
import { StellarAppKit } from '@saganta/stellar-appkit';
import '@saganta/stellar-appkit-ui-web';

// connectors is optional — defaults to Freighter, Albedo, xBull, Ledger
// domain + uri are optional too — auto-derived from window.location in the browser
const appkit = new StellarAppKit({
  network: 'TESTNET',
  appMetadata: { name: 'Example App' },
});

const modal = document.querySelector('stellar-appkit-modal');
modal.client = appkit;
modal.open();
```

Zero-config:
- `connectors` — omit to auto-register Freighter + Albedo + xBull + Ledger via `defaultConnectors()`
- `appMetadata` — v1.5.0+ follows the WalletConnect/Reown metadata standard: `{ name, description?, url?, icons? }`. Only `name` is required. `url` is derived from `window.location` if omitted (browser). In SSR, pass `url` explicitly. The same object is used for SIWS messages (domain derived from url, uri = url), WalletConnect session proposals, and the modal's transaction preview app icon (icons[0]).

Animation config (optional — defaults are sensible):
- HTML attributes: `animation="implode"` or `animation-open="slide-left" animation-close="fade"`
- Programmatic: `new StellarAppKit({ ..., modal: { animation: 'scale-blur' } })`
- Priority: HTML attrs > config > mode-based default
- `close(skipAnimation?: boolean)` — pass `true` to skip the WAAPI exit animation (used internally by drag-to-dismiss)

## SorobanConnection

```ts
import { SorobanConnection, Networks } from '@saganta/stellar-appkit';

const soroban = new SorobanConnection({
  rpcUrl: 'https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org',
  networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET,
  wallet: appkit,
});

// One call: build → simulate → prepare → sign → submit → poll
const result = await soroban.invoke({ contractId, method: 'transfer', args });

// Preview with balance deltas + fee estimate
const preview = await soroban.previewInvoke({ contractId, method: 'transfer', args });

// Typed contract client
const token = soroban.contract<TokenContract>('C...', { specEntries });
await token.transfer({ from, to, amount: 100n });
```

## SIWS

### Manual sign-in (client-side)

```ts
const { message, signedMessage, signerAddress, signedData } = await appkit.signIn({
  statement: 'Sign in to My App',
  nonce: await fetch('/api/siws/nonce').then(r => r.text()),
});
// POST { message, signedMessage, signerAddress, signedData } to your backend
```

### Server-side verification

```ts
import { verifySiws } from '@saganta/stellar-appkit-siws-verify';
const result = await verifySiws(
  { message, signedMessage, signerAddress, signedData },
  { expectedDomain: 'app.example.com', expectedNonce }
);
// result.ok → result.claims.address is the authenticated user
// !result.ok → result.reason explains why (enable debug: true for diagnostics)
```

### Automatic SIWS flow (v1.4.0+) — pass a SiwsConfig to StellarAppKit

The modal automatically runs the full SIWS flow right after the user connects a wallet: session check → nonce → sign → verify. The SDK manages the session lifecycle (persistence, expiry, sign-out, re-authentication).

```ts
const appkit = new StellarAppKit({
  network: 'TESTNET',
  appMetadata: { name: 'My App', url: 'https://app.example.com' },
  siws: {
    statement: 'Sign in to My App',
    session: async () => {                          // check for existing server session
      const res = await fetch('/api/siws/session');
      return res.ok ? res.json() : null;            // return SiwsSession to skip sign-in
    },
    nonce: async () => {                            // fetch server-issued nonce
      const { nonce } = await fetch('/api/siws/nonce').then(r => r.json());
      return nonce;
    },
    verify: async (data, nonce, ctx) => {           // verify server-side, return SiwsSession
      const res = await fetch('/api/siws/verify', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ ...data, nonce }),
      });
      return res.ok ? res.json() : null;            // ctx has { address, network } (v1.7.0+)
    },
    signout: async () => {                          // clear server session
      await fetch('/api/siws/logout', { method: 'POST' });
      return true;
    },
    refresh: async () => {                          // optional — refresh before expiry
      const res = await fetch('/api/siws/session');
      return res.ok ? res.json() : null;
    },
    disconnectOnFail: true,    // disconnect wallet if user closes modal before SIWS succeeds
    signoutOnDisconnect: true, // call signout() before clearing wallet session
    maxRetries: 3,             // show "Too many attempts" after 3 failures
    timeoutMs: 15_000,         // 15s timeout for nonce() and verify()
  },
});
```

### SIWS session lifecycle methods (v1.7.0+) — on the StellarAppKit client

- `appkit.siwsSession` — getter, returns SiwsSession | null, auto-clears expired
- `appkit.setSiwsSession(session | null)` — manually set/clear, persists to localStorage, emits siwsSessionChange
- `appkit.clearSiwsSession()` — clears session + storage, calls signout() per config
- `appkit.signOut()` — clears session + disconnects wallet (for "Log out" buttons)
- `appkit.requireAuth()` — throws ConnectError if not authenticated (guard privileged actions)
- `appkit.validateSession()` — re-checks against server via refresh() or session(), clears on mismatch
- `appkit.reauthenticate()` — clears session + emits siwsSessionChange:null (triggers fresh sign-in)

### SIWS session persistence (v1.7.0+)

Sessions are persisted to localStorage and restored on appkit.restore() (called by the React provider on mount). Survives page reloads — no re-sign needed on refresh.

### SIWS React hooks (v1.7.0+)

```tsx
import { useSiwsSession, useIsAuthenticated } from '@saganta/stellar-appkit-ui-web/react';
const session = useSiwsSession();          // reactive SiwsSession | null
const isAuthenticated = useIsAuthenticated();  // reactive boolean
```

### SIWS events

`siwsSessionChange` event fires with SiwsSession | null on set/clear/expire.

### SiwsError (v1.7.0+) — discriminated error type

```ts
type SiwsErrorType = 'session-check-failed' | 'nonce-fetch-failed' | 'sign-rejected' | 'verify-failed' | 'session-mismatch' | 'session-expired' | 'timeout' | 'max-retries-exceeded' | 'cancelled';
```

## Internationalization (i18n) — v1.8.0+

The entire modal UI is translatable into 25 locales. English is bundled by default; 24 additional locales are lazy-loaded via dynamic import() on first use.

Supported locales: en (bundled), zh-CN, zh-TW, es, pt-BR, ja, ko, de, fr, ru, ar (RTL), hi, it, tr, pl, vi, id, uk, nl, th, he (RTL), cs, sv, ro, fa (RTL).

```ts
// Set at initialization
new StellarAppKit({ locale: 'zh-CN', ... });

// Change at runtime (async — lazy-loads the locale)
import { setLocale, getLocale, t, onLocaleChange } from '@saganta/stellar-appkit';
await setLocale('ja');
t('title.connect_wallet');  // → 'ウォレットを接続'

// React hooks
import { useLocale, useSetLocale } from '@saganta/stellar-appkit-ui-web/react';
const locale = useLocale();
const setLocale = useSetLocale();
```

Uses intl-messageformat for ICU MessageFormat: {walletName} interpolation, {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} pluralization with CLDR-compliant rules per locale (Arabic has 6 forms, Russian has 4, Chinese has 1). Arabic-Indic digit localization (1 → ١ in Arabic).

## Error Handling

ConnectError with SEP-43 codes: -1 (internal), -2 (external service), -3 (invalid request), -4 (user rejected).
NetworkMismatchError subclass with expectedNetwork and actualNetwork.

## AI Integration

The library repo ships two AI-readable files at its root so AI coding tools (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Windsurf, Continue) can pick up the full API surface without you having to paste docs into chat:

- SKILL.md — Structured AI skill file with YAML frontmatter (name, description, license) and a body covering trigger conditions, install commands, common code patterns (basic connection, signing, Soroban, typed client, SIWS, React hooks), API reference tables, connectors table, per-wallet SIWS signing table, theming, and links. Used by skill-aware agents.
- llms.txt — Compact plain-text API index (~250 lines) following the llms.txt convention at https://llmstxt.org/. Sections: header, install, quick start, wallet connection, signing, Soroban, SIWS verification, framework wrappers, transaction preview, theming, error handling, tree-shaking, links. Read by any agent that reads repo files.

Raw URLs:
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sagantaHQ/stellar-appkit/main/SKILL.md
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sagantaHQ/stellar-appkit/main/llms.txt

This docs site also serves its own:
- https://stellar-appkit.saganta.com/llms.txt — compact index of every docs page
- https://stellar-appkit.saganta.com/llms-full.txt — full docs content concatenated (this file)

Recommended agent workflow:
1. Install the package first — once it is in package.json, agents can read llms.txt from node_modules/@saganta/stellar-appkit/llms.txt
2. Point the agent at the raw SKILL.md URL for trigger conditions and common patterns
3. For Soroban work, also point the agent at the typed-client docs page or the Soroban section of llms-full.txt
4. For SIWS verification, always have the agent read the SIWS docs page — the multi-candidate verification logic is subtle

Full AI Integration docs: https://stellar-appkit.saganta.com/reference/ai-integration/
